scope: 27.5-second perceptually plausible synthetic flower-arranging robot demo
summary: A source-state-locked, reviewed VFM route is DISPLAY_READY for synthetic visual use: official Wan2.2-Animate windows repair the high-risk late interval, deterministic hard routing avoids double anatomy, and the corrected adversarial critic plus high-resolution review pass the scoped display contract.
evidence: The final H.264 artifact decodes 660/660 frames at 1280x720, 24 FPS, and 27.5 seconds; SHA-256 is d9a00c72c13a623d04ca0eeeb625c0179ff3f04ef2dc87a4a6409d0d7320f886.

The lossless post-decode audit reports flower exactness 1.0, native-background exactness 0.9924290933, editable-support changed fraction 0.7355295522, and flower dynamic transition fraction 0.9800613497.

The corrected 720p adversarial audit evaluated all 660 frames, sampled or contact-attacked 585 frames, detected color/topology/contact/ghost attacks, and reports 20-second-and-later projected contact recall 1.0.
High-resolution review covered 24 uniform full frames plus 42 dense hand/seam frames and vetoed an optical-flow bridge because it visibly melted anatomy.

The compositor completed in 54.6897 seconds at 12.0681 FPS. Official 88-frame tail and bridge backend runs took 511.5277 and 476.9168 seconds; the persistent 660-frame incumbent took 509.7154 seconds.
lessons: For perceptual synthetic data, observed flower/background state should be immutable while foundation models resample only the uncertain robot layer.
Cross-dissolves and optical flow between incompatible identities create double or melted anatomy; deterministic hard routing is the safer bounded failure mode.

Critics need their own invariants: explicit logical ufuncs, bounded fractions, immutable input masks, and attackable-sample filtering prevented NumPy temporary reuse from producing false audit results.
Generated depth, telemetry, and forces are unnecessary for this display scope and must never be promoted as measurements.
limitations: The legacy all-in-one RGB-alpha image-space contract remains PARTIAL because late hand-replacement coverage violates its frozen anchor-derived limit on 23.33% of frames.
Frames 479 and 559 contain bounded one-frame route discontinuities visible under frame stepping.
The concurrent 566.2173-second scheduling path is derived from measured independent stages, not a separately timed end-to-end run.
No metric depth, calibrated camera, exact q/qdot, contact force, force closure, collision safety, or real-robot execution is established.
next_actions: Run the official late-window generators concurrently on disjoint leased GPUs to measure, rather than project, the 566.2173-second critical path.
Train or retrieve an identity-matched boundary bridge if frame-step continuity must become a hard display gate; do not use the rejected optical-flow bridge.
